title: How warfare changed

match.reason: The new point covers how warfare changed across the interwar and wartime period (tanks, aircraft, carriers, total war mobilisation and atomic bombs), and no bank point teaches that broader idea: the atomic bombs and trench warfare cards each cover only part of it.

draft.title: How warfare changed
card: World War I was mostly fought from trenches, where armies were stuck in long stand-offs. Between the wars, new machines made fighting faster and more mobile.
Tanks and fast-moving troops could break through enemy lines. Aircraft attacked soldiers, ships and cities from the air, far from the front line.
Aircraft carriers are warships that carry planes. They let navies strike from the sea at targets far away, as Japan did at Pearl Harbor in 1941.

Whole societies were turned to the war effort, with factories, workers and food supplies all used for it. In 1945 the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and Japan surrendered soon after.
draft.remember: Warfare moved from trenches to machines, drew in whole societies, and ended with atomic bombs.

a.q: Which change best describes how fighting in World War II differed from most fighting in World War I?
opts: Tanks and aircraft made fighting faster and more mobile
Armies dug longer trenches and stayed in them
Navies stopped being used because of aircraft
Fighting was limited to soldiers on a front line
a.why: Tanks and aircraft let armies move quickly and strike far from the front. Trench stand-offs were more typical of World War I, so longer trenches is the tempting wrong answer.
a.clue: Think about what machines let armies do.

b.q: In 1942, a factory in Melbourne switched from making cars to making aircraft parts, and its workers were directed to war jobs. What does this show about World War II?
opts: Whole societies were turned to the war effort
Fighting was confined to a distant front line
Trench warfare needed more heavy machinery
Atomic bombs had already ended the war
b.why: A factory changing its work to supply the war shows a whole society being used for the war effort. Atomic bombs came in 1945, at the end of the war, so they do not explain a 1942 factory.
b.clue: Look at who is helping the war besides soldiers.

a.best: Tanks and aircraft made fighting faster and more mobile

b.best: Whole societies were turned to the war effort
